source.title: Evaluating Instruction-Tuned Large Language Models on Code Comprehension and Generation
source.authors: Zhi-Qiang Yuan; Jun-Wei Liu; Qian-Cheng Zi; Ming-Wei Liu; Xin Peng; Yiling Lou

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares downstream task performance across model sizes, a different measure and setup from pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit scaling laws, or test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation. The rows capture its reported zero-shot comparisons within the Dolly and Vicuna size pairs, which bear on downstream predictability with scale. Other model-performance results are not recorded because they do not provide a separate within-family size comparison relevant to that version.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (instruction-tuned open models, zero-shot code tasks), the study compares 7B with 12B/13B checkpoints of the same family. Its stated observation that larger instructed models are not always better bears directly on V6. The test is weak: two size pairs, two points each, no fitted trend and no relation to pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that in zero-shot use, gains from larger scale are sometimes limited or even negative. Dolly performs much worse at 12B on assertion generation and code summarization. Vicuna-13B improves on generation tasks but has a small effect on classification. Scale is a side finding; the paper's main conclusions concern instruction tuning, few-shot prompting and fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: No original scaling-law method is reproduced; this is an evaluation of instruction-tuned models on downstream code tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors identify prompts, task and dataset selection, and evaluation metrics as potential limitations; they do not report these as factors affecting the size comparisons in the recorded rows.
record.problems: The relevant size comparisons cover only the Dolly 7B/12B and Vicuna 7B/13B pairs and four code tasks, not a broad scale sweep. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these comparisons and does not fit or test a predictive relationship. The authors also note that their findings may be limited by prompts, datasets, and evaluation metrics.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant size-comparison results were omitted.

untested.parts: No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fits in other regimes.
The study tests neither a predictive (fitted) relationship nor performance as a function of pretraining loss. It has only two sizes per family, so it cannot show predictability beyond direction.

record.verdict_notes: The record's blanket limits_scope label over r1-r8 is removed, because mixed results get separate condition-group labels. The rows_left_out claim of 'none omitted' is wrong: one-shot size comparisons (Tables V and VI) are unrecorded. Fine-tuned results for 12B/13B models are not reported in Table IX. The Dolly and Vicuna pairs differ only in size within each family, but the families use different bases (Pythia, LLaMA). Code summarization relies on a ChatGPT-judge metric over only 100 test items, with no uncertainty reported.

rows.subject: Dolly-12B

rows.note: The larger checkpoint has a slightly higher reported score.
rows.check: A 33.1 to 33.8 gain is a small move in the right direction, not a full effect. Authors call the Vicuna classification effect small; Dolly's DD gain is similarly marginal.

relationships.condition: Vicuna 7B to 13B, zero-shot generation tasks (assertion generation, code summarization)
relationships.reason: The larger model scores higher on both: EM 10.1 to 12.0 (r7) and preferred rate 48 to 63 (r8).
relationships.display_finding: The larger model increased assertion exact match from 10.1 to 12.0 and code summarization preference rate from 48 to 63.

relationships.condition: Dolly 7B to 12B on defect and clone detection; Vicuna 7B to 13B on clone detection, all zero-shot
relationships.reason: Gains with scale are only marginal: +0.7 accuracy (r1), +2.2 F1 (r2), +0.9 F1 (r6).
relationships.display_finding: Dolly gained 0.7 accuracy points on defect detection and 2.2 F1 points on clone detection, while Vicuna gained 0.9 F1 points on clone detection.

relationships.condition: Dolly 7B to 12B on assertion generation and code summarization; Vicuna 7B to 13B on defect detection, all zero-shot
relationships.reason: The larger model scores lower: EM 1.9 to 1.0 (r3), preferred rate 12 to 5 (r4), accuracy 54.0 to 49.8 (r5).
relationships.display_finding: Dolly assertion-generation exact match fell from 1.9 to 1.0 and code-summary preference rate from 12 to 5, while Vicuna defect-detection accuracy fell from 54.0 to 49.8.
